_comment: A Time page for the default scene. We have essentially none of this today:
of 35 candidate time words, `vocabulary.json` has two - `wait` and `again` -
and neither is really a time word.
The gap is not cosmetic. Without it a child cannot place anything in time:
no 'I want to go to the park tomorrow', no 'we saw grandma yesterday', no
answering 'when?'. Every reference board carries this behind a TIME or WHEN
link - Vocal Flair has a 46-word Time page, and Aubrey's device has TIME in
its top row of folders.
DELIBERATELY NOT A COPY OF THEIRS. Vocal Flair's Time page is built for an
adult: recent, current, brief, since, past, present, future, o'clock,
lately, season. Those are the words of someone discussing time, not a child
living in it. This takes the concrete end and leaves the abstractions.
`birthday` is deliberately absent. It was removed from the product in
August 2026 along with the child's date of birth, and a Time page is
exactly where it would creep back in.
ON COLOUR. There is no `adverb` case in PartOfSpeech - the codebase files
adverbs under `describe`, which resolves to adjective/blue (PartOfSpeech.swift
notes that `describe` 'mixes adjectives with adverbs'). So most of tier 1
comes out blue, the nouns orange, and before/after grey. That is correct
Fitzgerald behaviour for a category page, where a single colour is not the
goal the way it is in a home-page cluster.
Whether `adverb` should become a real case is a separate decision. It is
additive and low risk - PartOfSpeech is derived rather than stored on a
synced model, and a TileColorMap that has never heard of it simply has no
override for it - but it is not required for this page to ship.

clusters.name: tier 1 — when something happens, relative to now (blue: filed as describe)
tier 1 — parts of a day (orange: nouns)
tier 2 — ordering a sequence of events (blue)
tier 3 — frequency, the most abstract of the set (blue)

already_have._comment: Placed on the Time page too, by explicit key rather than class, because both currently live elsewhere.

new_words._comment: Each needs a vocabulary.json entry AND a parts_of_speech.json entry, or it falls back to its word class and draws the wrong colour. wordClass drives which page a word can be pulled onto; partOfSpeech drives colour.

art_notes._comment: Time is the hardest art brief this project has had, because none of it has a referent to draw. Worth deciding before generating anything.
art_notes.drawable: today / tomorrow / yesterday / week / weekend read well as a calendar with a highlighted cell - the convention every symbol set uses, and children learn it.
art_notes.day_parts: morning / afternoon / night / tonight are a sun-and-sky scene at different positions. These are the easy ones.
art_notes.hard: now / later / soon / before / after / first / next / last / always / never / sometimes have no picture. Symbol sets draw them as a clock face with a region marked, or as arrows on a timeline. Both are conventions to be taught rather than pictures to be recognised.
art_notes.alternative: Letters and numbers already skip generation and use GlyphTile. A text-forward treatment for the abstract half is worth considering rather than generating art that teaches nothing.
